nativeRepeatDiagnostics.explanation: SIZZLE, CLATTER and STOCK native Web Audio renders fail zero-tolerance comparison even when rendering the unchanged original twice. They remain explicit diagnostic failures, not passes; no sound implementation was modified.

limitations: PCM comparisons cover authored presets and representative rates/block sizes, not every possible patch or hardware configuration.
Native Web Audio self-variation prevents a bit-identical output claim for SIZZLE, CLATTER and STOCK; their full sound implementation, assets, controls and scheduler source remain identical.
UI call-site source equality does not alone prove runtime call cadence; independent application browser checks cover playback, inputs, view changes and microphone diagnostic cadence.

sampling.scope: Only UI waveform analysis caches and redundant UI painting/class updates. No audio implementation changes.
sampling.audioSourceVerification: git diff --quiet checkpoint -- all four audio engines, schemas, presets, BATTER adapters and complete sample libraries exited 0
sampling.benchmarksNote: Desktop Chromium medians for 100 redraws per trial, five trials; focused redraw costs, not whole-app CPU or mobile claims. STOCK and BATTER use original 20 s / 48 kHz stereo fixtures. STOCK waveform visible 766 x 216 px. DICER uses the unchanged factory sample. Machine load causes timing variation.

audit.problem: All four waveforms were repainted every animation frame even while stopped or while identical playhead meter data was repeated.
audit.change: WeakMap per canvas remembers every exact visual input: deck index, width, height, peaks, asset presence, trim, selection, playing, and clamped position. Reels, meters, audio and transport keep running as before.
audit.proof: Byte-identical audio sources; exact first-paint canvas pixels and unchanged waveform repeated draw produces zero canvas commands.

audit.problem: Schema normalization replaces the asset descriptor at every knob edit, making the UI recompute waveform peaks even though decoded sample PCM is unchanged. Idle step and pending-bank classes were rewritten every frame.
audit.change: Cache keys use decoded PCM identity, with original 700-bin algorithm unchanged. Class updates run when step, pending bank or playing state changes.
audit.proof: 500 benchmark full-sample rescans become zero; engine setState, DSP and sequence remain identical; exact canvas pixels.

audit.problem: Every trim marker move or control refresh recomputed both-channel per-pixel min/max decimation.
audit.change: WeakMap keyed by immutable decoded left-channel audio caches exact original min/max bins. Right-channel identity, width and zoom endpoints invalidate it; trim and loop overlays still repaint.
audit.proof: Exact original decimation operation order. Canvas pixels and all 216 source command cases identical across zoom, DPR and changing overlays.

audit.problem: Every trim pointer move scanned the entire left-channel decoded sample before repainting the unchanged waveform.
audit.change: WeakMap caches the identical original peak bins for decoded audio identity and bin count. Sample change or responsive width change invalidates it; trim controls and audio editing unchanged.
audit.proof: Exact peak amplitudes, source PCM never mutated, before/after canvas PNG equality and source checks.

skipped: DSP math reordering, coefficient approximations, oscillation/filter changes, sample-rate reduction, resampling, voice limits, timing/scheduler changes and source sample truncation were excluded because sound preservation takes precedence.
BATTER meter-array reuse was examined and skipped: its 1 KB per scheduler tick allocation has little impact and touching the engine adds unnecessary verification surface.
Existing decoded PCM and prepared-sample caches were retained with their current audio ownership and invalidation semantics; no budgets were altered.

interpretation: 337 deterministic production-DSP scenarios and two BATTER native Web Audio scenarios compare exactly with zero tolerance.
Three native Web Audio engines show numerical repeat-render variation in the unchanged baseline; strict native byte comparisons are documented as failures, not relaxed or presented as passed.
Every protected sound source and ordered audio/control/getter call expression is unchanged.
Interface benchmarks describe the measured display workload, not whole-app CPU usage or audio-processing speed.
Browser recording regression uses a synthetic MediaStream input and does not measure a physical interface or guarantee cross-device latency.
